note: Plain-English help for the page. Each entry: title, text, optional law (section ids to open), optional match (words to annotate in results) and annotate ("text" for claim text, "summary" for the summary line). Where the Acts define a term, the text says so and points to the section instead of restating thresholds.

sole_proprietor.title: Sole proprietor
sole_proprietor.text: A business owned and run by one person, with no separate legal existence from its owner. The owner is usually taxed personally on the profits.

company.title: Company
company.text: A business registered as a legal body separate from its owners, for example a limited company. The company itself is taxed on its profits.

partnership.title: Partnership
partnership.text: A business owned by two or more people who share its profits and losses without forming a company. Each partner is usually taxed personally on their share.

sector.title: Sector
sector.text: What your business mainly does, for example retail, restaurant, transport or software. Type it in your own words.

lga.title: Local government area
lga.text: The local council area where your business operates, for example Ikeja or Surulere. Local rules are not loaded yet, so for now this mainly records where you are.

turnover.title: Annual turnover
turnover.text: The total money your business takes in from sales over a year, before costs are taken off. Pick the band that fits your last full year. Some tax rules depend on how big a business is.

fixed_assets.title: Total fixed assets
fixed_assets.text: Things the business owns and uses over many years, such as buildings, vehicles, machinery and equipment. Stock you sell does not count. Some rules look at assets as well as turnover when deciding if a business is small.

employees.title: Employees
employees.text: How many people work for you on a payroll. If you have employees, rules about deducting tax from their pay can apply to you.

premises.title: Business premises
premises.text: Whether you work from a shop, office, workshop or other fixed place. Some charges depend on having premises.

signage.title: Signage
signage.text: Whether you display a sign or billboard for the business. Signage fees are usually set by state or local government, which are not loaded yet.

supported.title: Applies to you
supported.text: The law's own words, quoted under “Show the quote and why”, support this line for a business like yours.

qualified.title: Applies with a condition
qualified.text: The law applies, but a condition in the text, such as a size limit, could change the result for you. Read the condition in the details.

obligation.title: Obligation
obligation.text: Something the law says your business must do or pay.

exemption.title: Exemption
exemption.text: A case where the law says a rule does not apply to your business, so you do not have to do or pay it.

struck.title: Rejected by the check
struck.text: The Critic compared this line with the law's own words and found the text does not support it. The summary calls these “struck”. Read the reason to see why.

unchecked.title: Not verified
unchecked.text: The check could not be completed for this line, for example because a step failed. The summary calls these “could not be verified”. It is not a rejection; treat the line as unconfirmed.

vat.title: VAT
vat.text: Value Added Tax: a tax added to the price of most goods and services. Businesses collect it from customers and pay it to the government. Whether you must register or charge it can depend on your size. The law defines the details; open the section to read it.

paye.title: PAYE
paye.text: Pay As You Earn: the system where an employer takes income tax out of staff pay and pays it to the tax authority. The law sets out the employer's duties; open the section to read it.

tax_id.title: Tax ID
tax_id.text: Your tax identification number, issued by the tax authority. It is used on tax returns and other tax documents. The law says who must register; open the section to read it.

personal_income_tax.title: Personal income tax
personal_income_tax.text: Income tax charged on a person's income, including profits from a business they own personally. The law defines how it is worked out; open the section to read it.

companies_income_tax.title: Companies income tax
companies_income_tax.text: Income tax charged on the profits of a company, as opposed to a person. The law sets the rules; open the section to read it.

development_levy.title: Development levy
development_levy.text: A levy charged under the Tax Act on the profits of certain companies. Whether it applies depends on the kind and size of business. The law defines this; open the section to read it.

small_business.title: Small business
small_business.text: A size category used by the Tax Administration Act. The law defines it using limits on turnover and fixed assets, with some exceptions. The law defines this; open the section to read it.

small_company.title: Small company
small_company.text: A size category used by the Tax Act. The law defines it using limits on turnover and fixed assets. The law defines this; open the section to read it.

books_of_account.title: Books of account
books_of_account.text: Your business's records of money coming in and going out, such as sales, expenses and invoices, kept so that tax can be worked out. The law says what records must be kept; open the section to read it.
